mentl/2eea30b:
The parser correctly assigns handles starting at 1, and the inference engine synchronizes `graph_next_handle_g` to the parser's high-water mark. However, when `infer_walk_expr` encountered an `NHole` (tag 113) representing the `??` absence marker, it returned the literal constant `0` instead of returning its actual handle and binding it to `NFree`.

Because index 0 in the graph node array was never bound or initialized, any subsequent unification with that 0 handle caused `graph_node_at` to return `0` (an invalid `GNode` pointer). This triggered the `ka == 0` safety trap at the end of the `unify` dispatch logic.

This fixes the unreachable trap by properly binding `NHole` handles to `NFree(epoch)` and returning the actual AST handle, unblocking the M2 compiler bootstrap.

mentl/2e12329:
The root of the 12k pass-2 P_UnexpectedToken: lowering dropped a function
parameter's graph handle to 0 for every concrete-typed param. lower_param_handles
recovers the handle from the parsed TParam.ty, which only holds TVar(handle) while
the type is un-ground; once inference resolves it (String, Int, …) the handle is
gone and the lowered LLocal carries 0. A 0-handle local is type-blind, so `word ==
"fn"` cannot see word: String and emit type-dispatches `==` to pointer i32.eq
instead of str_eq — so keyword_kind's literal table never matches, every keyword
lexes as TIdent, and the parser can dispatch no statement.

The discipline's own rule (types.mn: never cache the resolved Ty; carry the handle
and live-chase): param_handles_of reads each param's handle from the fn's INFERRED
TFun, where build_param_types records it as TParam(name, TVar(h)). The local then
live-chases its type via lookup_ty, so every type-dispatched op (==, ++, to_string)
sees the type the graph proved. Falls back to lower_param_handles when the fn type
isn't a resolved TFun. Census holds at 173.

Seed mirror is the next gate: the seed's infer has no build_param_types, so its TFun
params carry no handle (tag-0 types) — the seed must thread the param handle into
its TFun before its lower can read it. Verdict B (the plan's prime suspect for the
12k) was right.
mentl/2e8c1bd:
Multi-line fn signatures are canonical SYNTAX.md form:
  fn lowpass_iir(input, cutoff, sr) -> Sample
      with Sample + Pure + !Alloc =
    let alpha = compute_alpha(cutoff, sr)
    (input * alpha) <~ delay(1)

The signature ends at TEq or TLBrace, period. TNewline is
whitespace within a signature, not a terminator.

Halting at TNewline was eager-form-commitment (chain-link 5):
the parser eagerly committed to single-line signatures and
bailed at TNewline, which then made the unfinished 'with' clause
+ body bleed past as separate stmts. The inner 'let alpha = ...'
surfaced as a TOP-LEVEL stmt; its name polluted
$ls_register_globals's input; $ls_is_global("alpha") returned
TRUE inside process_lowpass's handler-arm capture-resolution;
LGlobal($alpha) emitted; wat2wasm rejected as undefined global.

Substrate-honest: signature spans whatever lines it spans.
Closes the alpha leak that was masking 678 pre-existing
substrate errors (now visible).
